name: The Scarlet Letter
kicker: Hawthorne’s novel of Puritan Boston · Sin, shame, and secrecy
briefing: In Puritan Boston, Hester Prynne is forced to wear a scarlet “A” on her dress as punishment for having a child with a man who is not her husband. Nathaniel Hawthorne’s novel follows her daughter, Pearl, the mysterious physician Roger Chillingworth, and the guilt-ridden minister Arthur Dimmesdale as their secrets slowly come undone.
reject: the house of the seven gables

qb.tip: All 8 real tossups are Middle School/Easy High School, but most lean on Mistress Hibbins’s forest invitation and the meteor/Governor Winthrop scene rather than on Dimmesdale or Chillingworth by name.

sample.note: the 8 real QBReader tossups for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked)

tossups.p: This novel’s introductory essay, “The Custom-House,” claims that its author discovered a faded cloth emblem and an old manuscript while working at a Salem customhouse. Its heroine is first displayed on a scaffold holding her infant daughter before a crowd of Puritan onlookers.
tossups.r: That heroine must wear a mark of her sin, which she has embroidered herself. For 10 points, name this Nathaniel Hawthorne novel about Hester Prynne.

tossups.p: Mistress Hibbins, rumored to be a witch, invites this novel’s heroine to join a witches’ gathering in the forest outside town. Years later, that heroine meets her former lover in that same forest and briefly unpins her hair and removes her badge of shame.
tossups.r: Her daughter, Pearl, often plays alone near their isolated cottage. For 10 points, name this novel in which Hester Prynne raises her daughter alone in Puritan Boston.

tossups.p: Governor Winthrop’s death coincides with the sighting of a meteor that forms a dim red mark in the night sky, one that most townspeople read as a sign for “Angel” but that one guilt-ridden minister reads very differently. That same minister secretly whips himself and fasts in private.
tossups.r: He is the secret father of the heroine’s daughter, Pearl. For 10 points, name this novel in which the Reverend Arthur Dimmesdale hides his role in Hester Prynne’s disgrace.

tossups.p: This novel’s heroine is questioned on the scaffold by the elder minister John Wilson during her public punishment. An old scholar who arrives in town that same day disguises his identity and becomes the town physician.
tossups.r: That physician, Roger Chillingworth, is secretly the heroine’s long-lost husband, and he spends the rest of the novel tormenting her lover. For 10 points, name this novel set in Puritan Boston.

tossups.p: A jailer named Master Brackett oversees the heroine’s imprisonment early in this novel. Its heroine’s husband was presumed lost at sea before unexpectedly arriving in Boston in disguise, calling himself Roger Chillingworth.
tossups.r: Chillingworth lodges with the minister Arthur Dimmesdale in order to secretly torment him. For 10 points, name this novel about Hester Prynne’s public shaming in colonial Massachusetts.

tossups.p: This novel’s heroine is a gifted seamstress whose elaborate needlework decorates the very mark she is forced to wear. Over time, the Puritan community reinterprets that mark, deciding it stands for “Able” rather than for her original sin.
tossups.r: Her daughter, Pearl, is often described by other characters as an “elf-child.” For 10 points, name this novel by Nathaniel Hawthorne.

tossups.p: In this novel’s climax, a minister publicly confesses his hidden sin on a scaffold and reveals a mark on his own chest before dying in the heroine’s arms. Pearl kisses her father for the first time in this scene, finally acknowledging him.
tossups.r: That minister, Arthur Dimmesdale, had spent years secretly tormented by the physician Roger Chillingworth. For 10 points, name this Hawthorne novel that ends with Dimmesdale’s public death.

tossups.p: Roger Chillingworth dies within a year of this novel’s climax and leaves his entire fortune to young Pearl. Shortly before that climax, this novel’s heroine had planned to flee Massachusetts by ship with her lover after meeting him in the forest.
tossups.r: She eventually returns to Boston alone and resumes wearing her mark voluntarily, becoming a counselor to troubled women. For 10 points, name this novel whose heroine is buried near Arthur Dimmesdale under a shared tombstone.

tossups.p: This novel opens with a long essay describing the narrator’s time working at a Salem customhouse, where he claims to have found an old manuscript. Its heroine, publicly shamed for adultery, refuses to name her child’s father even under pressure from Governor Bellingham.
tossups.r: That heroine’s husband arrives in town in disguise, calling himself Roger Chillingworth. For 10 points, name this novel about Hester Prynne’s punishment in Puritan Boston.

tossups.p: In one scene, Mistress Hibbins invites this novel’s guilt-ridden minister to a witches’ gathering, much as she once invited its heroine. That minister had earlier imagined seeing a meteor spell out a message directly above him.
tossups.r: Arthur Dimmesdale eventually confesses that he is the father of Hester Prynne’s daughter. For 10 points, name this Hawthorne novel.

tossups.p: This novel’s physician character disguises his true identity after being presumed dead at sea, taking lodging with the very minister he intends to torment. That minister, wracked with guilt, secretly fasts and keeps a midnight vigil on the public scaffold.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this novel in which Roger Chillingworth seeks revenge on Arthur Dimmesdale, the secret lover of his wife, Hester Prynne.

tossups.p: This novel’s heroine is sentenced to stand on a scaffold before the entire Puritan community, holding her infant daughter, Pearl. A physician who lodges with the colony’s minister secretly works to uncover that minister’s hidden sin.
tossups.r: The minister, Arthur Dimmesdale, is secretly Pearl’s father. For 10 points, name this novel set in seventeenth-century Boston.

tossups.p: This novel’s elf-like young character, Pearl, grows up without knowing her father’s identity for most of the story. Her mother, publicly shamed for adultery, becomes a skilled seamstress whose needlework is admired even as she is shunned.
tossups.r: Pearl’s father, a minister named Arthur Dimmesdale, is secretly tormented by the physician Roger Chillingworth. For 10 points, name this novel by Nathaniel Hawthorne.

tossups.p: A meteor’s dim light forms a mark across the sky on the same night that this novel’s guilt-ridden minister holds a midnight vigil on the public scaffold. Townspeople interpret the meteor as marking the recent death of Governor Winthrop.
tossups.r: That minister, Arthur Dimmesdale, cannot bring himself to confess publicly until the novel’s climax. For 10 points, name this novel about Hester Prynne and her forced public shaming.

tossups.p: This novel follows a woman forced to wear an embroidered mark of her sin, who refuses to name her child’s father before the Puritan magistrates of Boston. Its central family stands together at last when a dying minister confesses on the town scaffold.
tossups.r: Hester Prynne raises her daughter, Pearl, alone while her husband, Roger Chillingworth, seeks revenge on her former lover. For 10 points, name this Nathaniel Hawthorne novel.

clues.t: Its heroine, Hester Prynne, is forced to wear an embroidered mark of her sin in public
A novel by Nathaniel Hawthorne, published in 1850
Hester’s daughter, Pearl, is often called an “elf-child” by other characters
The Reverend Arthur Dimmesdale is secretly the father of Hester’s daughter
Roger Chillingworth, Hester’s estranged husband, hides his identity under a false name and works as a physician to torment Dimmesdale
Set in Puritan Boston in the seventeenth century
The introduction, “The Custom-House,” frames the story as a manuscript found by the narrator in a Salem customhouse
Mistress Hibbins, a rumored witch, invites Hester (and later Dimmesdale) to a witches’ gathering in the forest
A meteor forms a dim red mark in the sky, read by the town as a sign for “Angel” marking Governor Winthrop’s death, but read by Dimmesdale as a sign of his own guilt
On the scaffold, Hester is questioned by the elder minister John Wilson
The jailer Master Brackett guards Hester during her imprisonment
Hester’s skilled needlework and charity later lead some townspeople to reinterpret her mark as standing for “Able”
The story proper opens with Hester displayed on a public scaffold holding her infant daughter
Governor Bellingham presides over the Puritan colony and presses Hester to name her child’s father
Hester and Dimmesdale meet secretly in the forest, where she briefly removes her mark and unpins her hair
The couple briefly plans to flee the colony together on a ship, but Dimmesdale confesses publicly instead
Dimmesdale publicly confesses and reveals a mark on his own chest before dying in Hester’s arms
Pearl kisses her father for the first time during his public confession, finally acknowledging him
Chillingworth dies within a year of Dimmesdale’s death and leaves his fortune to Pearl
Hester eventually returns to Boston alone and resumes wearing her mark voluntarily, counseling troubled women
Hester is buried near Dimmesdale under a shared tombstone marked with a red letter A on a black background

trap.title: Which man is which?
trap.body: Two secretive men in Hester’s life are easy to mix up. Arthur Dimmesdale is her lover and Pearl’s real father, a guilt-ridden minister who cannot bring himself to confess. Roger Chillingworth is her husband, who hides his identity and works as a physician to secretly torment Dimmesdale.
trap.fix: A clue about secret guilt, fasting, or a vigil on the scaffold means Dimmesdale. A clue about disguise, medicine, or revenge means Chillingworth. Either way, remember this whole tossup is usually asking for the novel itself, not either man.
trap.line: Real answer line: The Scarlet Letter (also accept its full original title, The Scarlet Letter: A Romance).

wrong: The House of the Seven Gables
